paragraphs: Children in care in Manchester are looked after by Manchester City Council's own fostering service and by the independent agencies listed on this page. The council is one of the ten Greater Manchester councils in Foster for Greater Manchester, a partnership run with the Greater Manchester Combined Authority to grow the number of foster carers. Enquiries made through the partnership get a reply within one working day.

The partnership says people of any age over 21, sexuality, gender, marital status, employment status, religion or background can foster. You need to be able to care for children, have a suitable home that you own or rent securely, and have good spoken and written English. In October 2023 the lead councillors for children's services in all ten councils signed a pledge to support their foster carers.

Manchester is looking for emergency foster carers who can take a child at short notice for up to two weeks while the council decides whether they can go home or need a longer-term family. The council says emergency carers receive up to £580 a week depending on the child's age, with a dedicated social worker and on-call help around the clock. Experience of children with emotional difficulties, for example from childcare, schools or residential care, is helpful.

Council carers also get a support team, local support networks, training and a route to progress. Agencies set their own fees and support, so compare the council with two or three of the agencies below before you choose.
